reason: Attack failed on the facts. The evidence URL the verifier named (tolkiengateway.net/wiki/Letter_213) is behind a Cloudflare interstitial and returns a 5 KB challenge page, not the letter, so the claim "Full text of the Carpenter selection, letter 213 read in place" overstates what was seen; a fan wiki would not carry the full text in any case. But the citation itself survives independent checking. Carpenter's heading for the letter is "213 From a letter to Deborah Webster 25 October 1958", and the sentence is printed "I am in fact a Hobbit (in all but size)." with Hobbit in italics, followed by "I like gardens, trees and unmechanized farmlands; I smoke a pipe, and like good plain food (unrefrigerated) ...". Number, recipient, date and wording therefore all hold; the only thing the card loses is the italic on Hobbit, which is typography, not wording. Gates: shipped.js returns shipped [] and near [], Tolkien at 1 for the year (month 5), cap 3, not banned, so no cap and no month collision. In scope: The Letters of J. R. R. Tolkien, ed. Humphrey Carpenter with Christopher Tolkien, 1981, comfortably before 2000; Correspondence is the form of the work and is in the closed vocabulary. Publishable, and on theme, since the whole point of the sentence is a man saying plainly what he is. Source line is 129 characters, under the 140 cap, leads with the author's name, has no dash and no straight double quote. Misattribution list checked: the Tolkien trap there is "Not all who wander are lost", which this is not. Two things the editor should fix rather than refuse: the evidence field should name the Carpenter volume as the text of record instead of the wiki page, and the empty note could usefully say that the letter answers a stranger's request for facts about him, which is why the self-description is so flat and literal.
